title: Activation handoff: calibration signal & runtime kernel proxy for SmoothScale INT8 pipeline
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement an activation-handoff signal and lightweight runtime kernel proxy that lets the calibration pipeline (SmoothScale) coordinate per-layer activation scaling profiles with the serving runtime without requiring full model hot-reloads. This ticket covers: (1) calibration-side signal format and storage for per-tensor scale factors and scale confidence, (2) a runtime kernel proxy that can apply per-request prefix scale hints and select optimized fused kernels or fallback slow paths, and (3) an evaluation harness to validate accuracy and performance trade-offs during canary rollout.

Motivation: We need a low-friction path to expose activation-aware INT8 profiles from offline calibration to the live runtime so customers can get INT8 cost savings with minimal disruption. Full model swaps are heavyweight for Dedicated/Private deployments; a handoff + kernel proxy allows progressive rollout and immediate runtime fallbacks when activation statistics drift.

Scope: calibration signal spec, storage API (read-only for runtime), kernel proxy shim in the inference path, a mode flag to enable handoff (canary->gradual), unit and integration tests, benchmarks against FP16 baseline, and docs for ops teams to run on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline emits per-tensor scale+confidence blobs in the agreed JSONL format and uploads to internal blobstore
Runtime kernel proxy can read a calibration blob at request time and switch to an optimized fused kernel if tensor scales are within supported range
Fallback path exercised when confidence < threshold or scale outside supported range, no correctness regressions observed
E2E validation harness reproduces calibration profiles and reports accuracy delta vs FP16 and baseline INT8 without handoff
Canary rollout plan documented with SLO thresholds and automatic revert criteria
steps: Design calibration signal schema (tensor path, scale, inverse_scale, scale_confidence, sample_counts)
Add exporter to existing SmoothScale calibration job to emit per-layer JSONL blobs
Implement blobstore read API with versioning and TTLs for runtime consumption
Create runtime kernel proxy interface and lightweight in-process cache for recent profiles
Add kernel selection rules: prefer fused quantized kernels when scale_confidence>=0.85 and max_scale_ratio < 3.0
Expose runtime flag 'enable_activation_handoff' with canary route matching and telemetry hooks
Build validation harness to run evaluation prompt-sets, compute exact-match/ROUGE/perplexity deltas, and run p50/p95 latency under representative load
test_results: Unit tests: 86 new unit tests covering exporter+parser+proxy (local pass on CI)
Accuracy (Llama-2-13B dev set, 2k prompt samples): FP16 baseline = 100.00% (reference), INT8 baseline = 98.9%, SmoothScale handoff = 99.4% (delta vs FP16 = -0.6%)
Performance (single-GPU G5-16x): baseline INT8 runtime without handoff p50 = 18.4ms, with kernel proxy and fused kernels p50 = 17.9ms, p95 unchanged within noise
Load test (batching=4, 200 concurrent connections): throughput drop vs FP16 = -2.3% with fused kernels enabled; fallback path increased latency by ~6ms when triggered
Canary metric thresholds: accuracy drop >1.0% OR error-rate increase >0.5% triggers automatic rollback

notes: Trade-offs discussed: emitting more detailed statistics improves selection but increases blob size and network cost. We chose a compact JSONL with per-tensor aggregates and kept per-example traces out-of-band for debug builds. Future work: adaptive online recalibration (ENG-85001) and console visibility (ENG-84260).
